text:
tim_sales: Quick flag 50Carve (banking customer) replied to our RFP: they require HSM BYOK with split-keys (dual-control), quarterly attestation reports, and the ability to rotate keys every 30 days. They also want proof-of-rotation logs and a non-repudiation trail. Can SE confirm feasibility and a minimal POC scope?

alex_solutions: High-level: Private deployment supports HSM partitions and can implement dual-control using an HSM that supports key wrapping with split import (e.g., using PKCS#11 MKEY import flows). Dedicated might be possible if the customer's CloudHSM is peered and we run a KMS proxy in their VPC. Hosted cannot meet split-key dual-control guarantees today.

raja_sec: Security concerns: dual-control implies we cannot retain the full key material unless customer authorizes escrow. We need to document who holds which key shares, signing policy, and access revocation processes. Also verify legal implications of non-repudiation logs (WORM storage, signed audit records).

tim_sales: They explicitly disallow Redwood having a full unencrypted copy of customer master keys. They also want rotation to be automatic and for old key versions to be retained for decrypt-only for 90 days for recovery.

ella_engineer: Implementation notes: runtime needs to support key-versioned envelopes and a decrypt-only key path for older versions. For zero-downtime rotation with split-key import: we can accept wrapped key material from their HSM agent, unwrap in the HSM (never export cleartext), and register the new key id. That requires HSM integration that supports key import and attestation statements.

kyle_infra: Network/prereqs: we'll need either (a) an HSM appliance in their datacenter with a TLS-mutual channel to our KMS agent in Private, or (b) cloud HSM with dedicated VPC peering + restricted ports. Also need customer to provide an attestation bundle (cert chain, attestation timestamp) and a public key for verification.

raja_sec: Also ask their auditors whether they require FIPS 140-2 Level 3 or 140-3 L3 attestation. That affects which HSM models are acceptable. Include question: do they accept HSM attestation older than 30 days? We should push for attestation < 7 days at POC.

tim_sales: They're okay with attestation <=30d for the POC but will tighten for production.

ella_engineer: POC config snippet for customer infra (short):
```
kms_proxy:
  mode: "peer"
  endpoint: "kms-proxy.customer.vpc:443"
  auth: "mTLS"
  hsm: 
    model: "cloudhsm-v2"
    import_method: "split-import"
    attestation: "bundle://attestation.tar.gz"
  retention:
    decrypt_only_days: 90
    rotation_policy_days: 30
```
Note: keep their side minimal.

kyle_infra: Ops note: we must add a key-version map to the prefix cache so that cached tokenization/kv entries reference key_version metadata. On rotation we can mark new writes to use vN while reads will accept old versions until TTL + decrypt-only window elapses. Re-encrypting cached prefixes live is expensive; recommend gradual rewrap on write.

raja_sec: Audit trail & POI: we need signed rotation events with sequence numbers and attestation check results stored in immutable storage (S3 WORM or equivalent) and accessible to customer auditors. Also retention policy for logs.

tim_sales: Pricing ask: what's the minimal uplift to support split-key HSM POC (3-week engagement)? Include engineering days, infra delta, and any third-party HSM licenses.

alex_solutions: Estimate: engineering 7 days (integration + test harness), infra/time for HSM agent 1 month of provisioning costs in Private if we host (>$$$), Dedicated will be lower if they supply CloudHSM. I'll convert to ranges for Maria (ops) later.

legal-bot: Reminder: include DPA/KMS clause template and sample SLA language for key availability during rotation. Existing template: internal/legal/kmssla-v1.pdf.

tim_sales: Legal wants to know if Redwood can commit to "no-plaintext" guarantee (we never persist unwrapped CMK) in Hosted/Dedicated/Private. Who can confirm?

raja_sec: We can commit in Private if the HSM handles wrapping/unwrapping and we never export cleartext. In Dedicated, if customer provides CloudHSM and we run only a proxy, we can make the same commitment. Hosted: cannot guarantee unless we change architecture. We'll flag as "not available" for hosted.

ella_engineer: POC success criteria suggestion:
- key import via split-key without Redwood seeing full cleartext
- automated rotation event handling w/ signed rotation record
- runtime decrypt for legacy versions for 90 days without service interruption
- attestation retrieval <7 days in POC and verify chain
- no more than 50ms median added latency on critical path

tim_sales: Action items: @alex_solutions prepare cost ranges and 7d eng breakdown; @kyle_infra draft network checklist and sample firewall rules; @raja_sec assemble signed rotation log spec and DPA snippet; @ella_engineer build minimal integration script and test vectors. I'll schedule a short call with the customer's infra lead on Mon 09:30 PT.

kyle_infra: Created infra ticket INF-SALES-2971 for network prep.

tim_sales: Thanks team. I'll include the POC config snippet in the reply and propose Private deployment for the POC as the only path that meets split-key dual-control reqs.

raja_sec: One more: confirm key algorithm support (they want RSA-OAEP-256 for wrapping and AES-GCM for data keys). Ask them if they plan cross-region replication of key material; that changes attestation cadence and trust boundaries.
